summary.title: bliki: Test Pyramid
summary.one_liner: Learn why a balanced test portfolio should have many low-level unit tests and few slow, brittle end-to-end UI tests, and how service-layer tests fit in between.
takeaways: Write many fast, low-level unit tests and only a few broad-stack UI tests.
UI record-playback tests are slow, brittle, expensive to write, and prone to non-determinism.
Subcutaneous tests act through the service or API layer and avoid many UI framework complexities.
Treat high-level test failures as a sign of a missing unit test; reproduce the bug with a unit test before fixing it.
Test concerns like end-to-end, UI, and customer-facing are orthogonal and should not be conflated.
summary.summary: Martin Fowler's short bliki article describes the test pyramid, a model for balancing automated tests so most are low-level unit tests and few are broad-stack tests driven through a GUI. He explains why UI record-playback testing degrades into an "ice-cream cone": such tests are slow, need special licensing or machines, and are brittle when the system changes. He adds an intermediate layer of subcutaneous tests that act through a service or API layer, and notes that end-to-end, UI, and customer-facing tests are separate characteristics. The page closes with footnotes, further reading, and the history of the idea.
